explanation.text: A file is a piece of work saved on a computer, like a picture or a document. A folder is a place used to keep files organized together, just like a real folder holds paper.
explanation.example: You might save a drawing as a file, and keep all your drawing files together inside a folder called "My Drawings".

questions.prompt: What do we call a piece of work saved on a computer, like a picture or a document?

hints.small: Think about what you save when you finish a drawing or a document.
hints.big: Saved work like pictures and documents are called files.

explanationSteps: A file is a piece of saved work, such as a picture, document, or song.
So the answer is "A file".

questions.prompt: What do we call a place on the computer used to keep files organized together?

hints.small: Think about how you might group similar files together.
hints.big: A folder holds files together, just like a real paper folder.

explanationSteps: A folder is used to keep related files organized together.
So the answer is "A folder".

questions.prompt: If you have many drawing files, what is the best way to keep them organized?
options: Put them all in one folder named "Drawings"
questions.correctAnswer: Put them all in one folder named "Drawings"

hints.small: Think about what folders are used for.
hints.big: Grouping similar files into one folder makes them easy to find later.

explanationSteps: Folders help us group similar files together.
Putting all drawing files in a folder named "Drawings" keeps them organized.
So the answer is to put them all in one folder named "Drawings".

questions.prompt: Why do we save our work on a computer?
options: So we don't lose it and can open it again later
questions.correctAnswer: So we don't lose it and can open it again later

hints.small: Think about what happens to your work if you don't save it.
hints.big: Saving keeps your work stored so you can find and open it again.

explanationSteps: Saving stores your work as a file so it isn't lost.
You can then open that file again later to keep working on it.
So the answer is: so we don't lose it and can open it again later.

questions.prompt: What is the small picture on the desktop that you double-click to open a program or file called?

hints.small: You see these small pictures on the desktop before you open anything.
hints.big: Double-clicking one of these small pictures opens a program or file.

explanationSteps: An icon is a small picture that represents a program, file, or folder.
Double-clicking it opens what it represents.
So the answer is "An icon".

questions.prompt: What is the blinking line on the screen that shows where your typing will appear called?

hints.small: Look for the blinking line when you type in a document.
hints.big: This blinking line marks where the next letter you type will appear.

explanationSteps: The cursor is the blinking line that marks where typing will appear.
So the answer is "The cursor".

questions.prompt: Which of these is most like a real-world folder that holds paper files?

hints.small: Think about which of these is used to organize and hold things.
hints.big: A computer folder works just like a paper folder — it holds files together.

explanationSteps: A real paper folder holds papers together, just like a computer folder holds files together.
So the answer is "A computer folder".

questions.prompt: What should you do before turning off the computer, if you have unsaved work?

hints.small: Think about what happens to unsaved work if the computer turns off.
hints.big: Saving stores your work as a file so it isn't lost when the computer turns off.

explanationSteps: Unsaved work can be lost when the computer turns off.
Saving first keeps your work safe as a file.
So the answer is: save your work first.
